faq.q: Is now a good time to buy gold?
faq.a: Gold investment should align with your long-term asset allocation strategy rather than short-term market timing. Current dips might offer an entry point for those under-allocated to gold and looking to diversify their portfolio.

faq.q: How does a strong US dollar affect gold prices?
faq.a: A strong US dollar makes gold more expensive for investors holding other currencies, which can reduce demand and put downward pressure on gold prices in international markets.

SGBs are government securities denominated in grams of gold. They offer an annual interest rate, are exempt from capital gains tax upon maturity for individuals, and eliminate the need for physical storage.

faq.q: Are gold ETFs better than physical gold?
faq.a: Gold ETFs offer convenience, high liquidity, and no storage costs, unlike physical gold. They also track gold prices closely and can be bought/sold on stock exchanges like shares, making them a popular digital alternative.

Gold is traditionally considered a hedge against inflation. When inflation rises, the purchasing power of currency erodes, and investors often turn to gold to preserve their wealth and protect against rising costs.

faq.q: What is the tax treatment for Gold ETFs and Gold Mutual Funds?
faq.a: For Gold ETFs and Gold Mutual Funds, capital gains are taxed based on the holding period. Short-term capital gains (held for 36 months or less) are added to your income and taxed as per your slab, while long-term capital gains (held for more than 36 months) are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in gold in India?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can invest in various forms of gold in India, including physical gold, Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs), and Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), subject to FEMA regulations.
